decision_reason: IASO is a Bluesquare-developed georegistry, campaign-microplanning and field data-collection platform, and its first-party README explicitly attributes its creation to the private company. The DRC, Niger, Cameroon and other public-health deployments are evidence of public-sector use, not government creation, commissioning or sponsorship of the software. Its public source, MIT grant, first licensed-source year, current documentation and operational use were separately checked. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The canonical project's README says IASO was created by Bluesquare and became open source under MIT in November 2020. Its account of public-health campaigns and validation by public officials describes use and implementation, not a government agency's product-specific creation, funding, commissioning or stewardship. No government-origin link for the platform itself was found.

public_source.note: This is the public canonical repository for the actual IASO web/backend and frontend source, with development, test, build, deployment, and API material. The official docs describe installation and use; the repository history is active and the README documents production image build and deployment.

eligible_license.note: The repository's direct root grant is the complete MIT License, an OSI-approved license for first-party IASO repository source. Dependencies and reused ODK components retain their own notices; MIT is not attributed to those external materials.

primary_evidence.note: Bluesquare's current product-specific account documents a 2026 IASO implementation with Cameroon's Expanded Programme on Immunization for field verification in a campaign; the official product documentation supplies setup and user guidance. The creator's five-year account documents earlier multi-country deployments and product metrics. This establishes current operational use and notability, but not government provenance.

decision_reason: OpenHEXA is a multi-repository public-health data integration and analysis platform developed by private company Bluesquare. Public agencies use it and some projects deploying it receive public funding, but those implementation relationships do not establish that an agency created, commissioned, funded or stewarded the OpenHEXA product itself. The assigned repository is explicitly a no-code installer/bootstrap repository; the actual core app and notebooks source are publicly available separately. The component license boundaries were recorded conservatively. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The canonical README says OpenHEXA is developed by Bluesquare; the assigned repository is a product/bootstrap package. Official accounts document Ministry of Health deployments in Niger and Côte d'Ivoire, including an instance in a USAID-supported activity, but these are deployment/project relationships and do not show public-agency origination or sponsorship of the OpenHEXA platform itself.

public_source.note: The assigned BLSQ/openhexa repository explicitly says it contains no application code and points users to the technical architecture. That first-party architecture identifies the public openhexa-app core and openhexa-notebooks component; both source repositories are accessible at https://github.com/BLSQ/openhexa-app and https://github.com/BLSQ/openhexa-notebooks. The platform source is therefore public, but distributed across repositories rather than contained in the assigned lead.

eligible_license.note: The actual core app has a direct MIT grant and the separate notebooks component also identifies MIT. The MIT file in the assigned no-code bootstrap repo does not cover linked components. Because the OpenHEXA platform is split among the app, notebooks, SDK, toolbox and image repositories, a complete component-by-component license/scope map was not established in this tranche; no product-wide MIT claim is made.

primary_evidence.note: The official Bluesquare account dated August 2026 describes the exact OpenHEXA platform as the integration/orchestration layer in a live national HIV-data system in Côte d'Ivoire, in partnership with the Ministry of Health and supported through a USAID-backed activity. Current documentation provides user, administrator and installation guidance. This is strong current use/notability evidence only; it does not establish product provenance.

product_identity: OpenHEXA, a multi-repository open-source data integration, analytics, notebook and pipeline platform; the assigned BLSQ/openhexa repo is an installer/bootstrap repository, not the application source
agency: No government-originating agency identified; developed by private company Bluesquare (Blue Square SA). Ministries of Health in Niger and Côte d'Ivoire are documented implementation partners/users.
geography: Belgium (developer origin); public-health deployments documented in Niger and Côte d'Ivoire; globally installable
license: MIT for first-party core application and MIT for the separately licensed notebooks component; other platform repositories and external dependencies require their own scope review
status_note: The 2021-02-11 MIT-license commit in the public core-app history follows implementation code in January 2021; the 2022 assigned bootstrap repository's creation date is not used as the product source year. Current official deployment and user/installation docs pass notability. The platform source is multi-repo and no product-wide grant is asserted. No exact GOSDIR catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: Bonita has strong product-specific government-research provenance: Inria's ECOO team records the workflow system and dates its first LGPL release to 2004. The current Bonita Engine source and Community Edition documentation are public and current. Hold because the assigned URL is the Bonitasoft GitHub organization, not a product repository, and official documentation says Community Edition is composed of multiple component repositories. The complete component/license boundary for the exact product is not yet established, so it is not ready to publish as a product-wide entry. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: Inria's official ECOO project-team report identifies Bonita as its flexible workflow management system, lists ECOO participants, and states that its first version was released in 2004 under LGPL. The report also locates ECOO in the LORIA joint research environment. The current Bonitasoft Engine repository is an official successor component of the named Bonita product; later commercial stewardship does not erase the specific public-research origin.

public_source.note: The canonical Bonita Engine repository is public, active and contains actual runtime source, tests and build instructions. Official Bonita documentation states that the Community Edition source is available in the Bonitasoft GitHub organization and that each component has its own repository; the assigned URL itself is an organization page rather than one canonical source repository.

eligible_license.note: The current Bonita Engine root grant is LGPL-2.1; Inria's official reports describe the 2004 release as LGPL and a 2005 ObjectWeb distribution as GPL, both OSI-approved. However, the assigned organization contains many repositories and editions with different scopes; the full Community Edition component/license boundary, distinct from Subscription-edition material, was not verified component by component. No single organization-wide license is inferred.

primary_evidence.note: Current versioned Bonita documentation provides product and developer guidance; official docs describe Community Edition installation/distribution and building from source. The public engine repo has current development. This meets the operational tool and user-documentation baseline for the product family while the exact multi-repository scope remains on hold.

product_identity: Bonita Community Edition, a multi-component digital process automation/business process management platform; the canonical Bonita Engine is its runtime component
agency: Inria Project-Team ECOO at LORIA (public research origin); subsequent product stewardship passed through Groupe Bull and Bonitasoft
geography: France (ECOO/LORIA origin); global workflow automation product
license: The first Bonita release was LGPL-licensed per Inria; current Bonita Engine uses LGPL-2.1. Other Community Edition components and subscription-only material have distinct repository/license scopes not fully mapped here.
status_note: The source year is the contemporaneous Inria report's first release date, not the current vendor repository's import date. Inria's 2005 report calls the ObjectWeb distribution GPL while its 2008 report specifies LGPL for the first 2004 release and Nova Bonita; both grants are OSI-approved. Hold is specifically for full product/component and edition scope, not lack of Inria provenance or current distribution. Exact catalog lookup found no duplicate.

decision_reason: Boxtribute is a humanitarian inventory/aid distribution application developed and operated by the independent Dutch Boxwise Foundation with volunteer developers, not a government agency. Government or humanitarian-sector use does not establish government product provenance. The actual public source, Apache-2.0 grant/scope, first licensed-source year, current product activity and documented partner use were checked. No exact catalog match found; no catalog entry added.

It does not identify a government creator, commissioning agency, product funder or steward. Humanitarian/charity use is not government provenance.

public_source.note: The assigned canonical repository contains the actual Boxtribute 2.0 humanitarian-aid web application source, setup and deployment files, docs, tests and active history. It is not just a registry entry or deployment configuration.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE.md is the direct Apache License 2.0 grant for the Boxtribute first-party codebase, an OSI-approved license. The foundation's 2020 report independently identifies that codebase as Apache-2.0; external dependencies retain their own notices.

primary_evidence.note: The current first-party site describes live aid-transfer functionality with partner organizations and ongoing product news; the foundation's activity report documents deployments and partner organizations. The current public source history and project website support current distribution/use plus an independently operated, documented product.
